title: Marigot SupplyPilot inference intake notes
content:
Meeting: Marigot (SupplyPilot) kickoff — 2024-11-18 (30m)
Attendees: Rhea (RDW SE), Jonas (RDW Solutions Eng), Marina (Marigot PM), Luis (Marigot infra lead), Claire (Marigot data)

High-level ask:
- Replace slow rule-based returns assistant with LLM-powered assistant to parse RMA requests, generate recommended return reasons, and surface next-step actions for ops team.
- Must run inside Marigot VPC/private deployment (sensitive returns data). SLA target: p95 < 250ms for single-shot routing calls; bulk processing can be batch-y.
- Cost target: keep per-interaction token cost under $0.06 equivalent (they have margin constraints).

Quick summary / positioning:
- They want a lightweight edge of the platform in their AWS VPC with private control plane. Likely Redwood Private (VPC) deployment + small Dedicated pool for steady throughput.
- Two primary workflows: 1) real-time chat/routing (low latency, single-turn), 2) async bulk enrichment (nightly batch for historical orders).

Technical notes captured during call:
- Data flow: app -> internal API -> Redwood Private endpoint (VPC) -> model. They expect to feed order metadata + short customer message. No PII direct fields but order ids and partial addresses present.
- Token budget: typical request ~300 tokens in + ~150 tokens generated. Need to optimize prompts and consider model choice + quantized variants.
- Preferred models: open-models preferred (cost) but acceptable to use a higher-perf checked model for routing step if latency required.
- KV cache opportunity: many flows repeat prefixes (same product/return reason combos). Suggest prefix/KV caching for common SKUs to cut token marginal cost.
- Batching: Nightly enrichment can use high-batch throughput on Dedicated cluster; real-time should avoid batching >1 for latency SLO but enable micro-batching if p99 latency allows.

Gotchas / risks flagged by Marigot:
- Security: their compliance team requires explicit KMS integration + audit log export to their S3. Need doc showing HSM/KMS compat and audit hooks.
- Network: egress rules in their VPC are restrictive — must validate private control-plane handshake flow and NAT requirements. Luis asked if we need egress to our telemetry endpoints.
- Model hallucination: ops team cannot tolerate wrong return reasons; they need confidence scores and an easy way to attach fallback to deterministic rules.
- Rate shaping: peak return bursts (end of month) can be 3–4x baseline. They want autoscale guarantees and a canary fallback to cheaper model when Dedicated pool saturated.

Preliminary requirements list (working):
- Private deployment (VPC) with option to place Redwood Private control plane in their account or via dedicated peering.
- Dedicated inference pool for real-time routes: target 300 RPS sustained at median 200ms token latency (call regs TBD).
- Nightly bulk job: process ~1.2M orders / day, prefer server-side batch runs using our Dedicated cluster with spot-like scaling for cost.
- KMS/HSM integration guide + audit log S3 export for compliance.
- Prompt templates + versioning: allow ops to pin templates; UI or config for rollout/canary.
- Post-process rule engine: simple webhook to call their deterministic rule-set for cases with low-confidence LLM outputs.

Initial architecture suggestions (quick sketches):
1) Real-time path: Marigot app -> internal API -> RDW Private VPC endpoint (pinned model: open-gpt-v1-q8 maybe) -> confidence threshold -> if score < 0.7 call fallback rule engine -> store decision in event log.
2) Bulk path: Push ndjson files to an S3 bucket (Marigot) that RDW Worker pulls through a secure role -> batch inference on Dedicated pool -> results written back to their S3.

Action items (owners + proposed dates):
- Rhea: produce 1-page VPC + network checklist for Marigot (include ports, NAT, endpoint IPs) — due 2024-11-22
- Jonas: run a quick cost sketch comparing open quantized model vs small proprietary model for 300 tokens in/150 out at target RPS — due 2024-11-25
- Marina: provide sample payloads (10 representative messages + order metadata) and a list of deterministic rule cases they will always override — due 2024-11-21 (received 2024-11-20 partial)
- Luis: share network CIDR and any egress restrictions + KMS contact — due 2024-11-21 (partial: sent CIDR, asked KMS contact pending)
- Claire: define acceptance criteria for "correct return reason" (ops labeling rubric) and provide 100 labeled examples if available — due 2024-11-29

Open questions / followups:
- Do they want us to host the control plane in their AWS account (customer-managed) or run a segregated tenant in our infra with private connectivity? Tradeoffs: onboarding speed vs compliance.
- Latency SLO exact numbers (they claimed p95 < 250ms) — need to measure baseline with chosen model on our Dedicated nodes. Jonas to run microbenchmarks.
- Can they accept partial PII in tokenized/hashed form? Claire to confirm with privacy/compliance.
- Which metrics do they want surfaced in Console? token-level cost breakdown, per-route latencies, and a per-decision confidence histogram were requested — confirm retention window.

Notes to self (Rhea):
- Emphasize prefix cache savings in next email with an example: SKU-level static prompt parts cached reduces avg tokens by ~30% in pilot workload (estimate).
- Prepare short demo script: 3 live examples (good match, ambiguous -> fallback, hallucination -> rule) to show in next call.
- Keep canary plan simple: start with 10% traffic to new model, fallback to deterministic engine if errors spike.

Meeting cadence suggested:
- Weekly 30m sync for first 6 weeks, ops/data/HW touchpoints as needed.
- Next checkpoint: 2024-11-25 internal demo of cost/latency sketches and network checklist.

Quick draft email points for Marina (do not send yet):
- Attach network checklist and minimal RBAC/KMS notes.
- Outline two-phase roll: pilot (3 weeks, 10k/day), then scale to daily batch.
- Ask for labeled sample set + failure modes.

Immediate next-step (today):
- Post partial cost sketch into Slack #se-marigot and ping Marina.
- Upload network checklist draft to Confluence (linked_artifact above).

---
Raw capture ends here — will convert to formal partner brief once we have sample payloads and the compliance contact.
